label: Meat & Protein
description: Fresh and frozen animal proteins including beef, poultry, pork, fish, and seafood.

automatic_checks.label: CFIA Fat-Tier Labeling
automatic_checks.rule: For ground beef/pork: Extra Lean = ≤10% fat, Lean = ≤17% fat. Product must display CFIA-compliant fat tier on label.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Product declares fat tier OR fat % is clearly stated on label
automatic_checks.flag_if_fail: Fat content not declared — cannot verify CFIA compliance

automatic_checks.label: Single Ingredient
automatic_checks.rule: Whole cuts (chicken breast, steak, fish fillet) must be single-ingredient with no brines, solutions, or flavor injections unless clearly labeled.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: Ingredients list shows meat only, OR injected % is declared
automatic_checks.flag_if_fail: Contains undeclared solution/brine — inflates weight, reduces protein density

automatic_checks.label: No Added Nitrates / Preservatives
automatic_checks.rule: Processed meats (deli, bacon, sausage) must be free of added sodium nitrate/nitrite. 'Cultured celery powder' counts as a source — flag it.
automatic_checks.pass_condition: No sodium nitrate, sodium nitrite, or celery powder/extract on ingredients
automatic_checks.flag_if_fail: Contains nitrates or celery extract (de facto nitrate source)

automatic_checks.label: Canadian Origin Preferred
automatic_checks.rule: Prefer products with 'Product of Canada' or 'Canadian' on label. Flag imports — not a disqualifier, but noted.
automatic_checks.flag_if_fail: Origin not Canadian or not declared — still return best available, flag clearly

certifications.label: Canada Organic (CFIA)
certifications.note: Only valid if certification body is listed on label. 'Natural' and 'hormone-free' are unregulated marketing terms — do not treat as equivalent.

certifications.label: Animal Welfare Approved / Certified Humane
certifications.logo_text: Certified Humane or Animal Welfare Approved
certifications.note: Informational only — not a disqualifier if absent, but surfaced as a bonus signal.

options.label: Grass-Finished
pros: Higher omega-3 fatty acids (2–4x vs. grain-finished)
No feedlot grain rations or growth promotants
cons: Harder to find at mainstream retailers (Walmart unlikely)
Canadian grass-finished supply is limited Oct–April
options.best_for: Nutrition-first, higher budget, willing to pay premium

options.label: Grain-Finished (Conventional)
cons: Higher omega-6 content, worse omega-3 ratio
May include feedlot practices depending on source
CFIA 'Lean' and 'Extra Lean' grades still apply — must verify fat tier

options.label: Wild-Caught
pros: No added astaxanthin dye (natural color from diet)
Higher omega-3 per 100g in most species
cons: Seasonal — frozen wild-caught is the year-round alternative
Texture can be firmer, less forgiving to cook

options.label: Farmed (Atlantic)
cons: Synthetic astaxanthin added for color (SalmoFan dye scale used)
Antibiotic use varies by farm — look for ASC or Ocean Wise
Higher omega-6 content from grain-based feed
PCB/contaminant levels historically higher than wild
options.best_for: Fresh fish preference, lower budget — prioritize ASC-certified

options.label: Free-Run / Free-Range
pros: Indoor floor access (free-run) or outdoor access (free-range)
Regulated term in Canada under Canadian Chicken Farmers guidelines
cons: Free-run ≠ organic — may still use conventional feed

options.label: Conventional
pros: Canadian supply chain is hormone-free by regulation (CFIA bans growth hormones in poultry)
options.best_for: Budget-first — note: all Canadian chicken is hormone-free regardless

edge_case_rules.no_qualifying_product: Return best available. Flag every failed criterion. Never omit the category.
edge_case_rules.no_canadian_origin: Flag as imported. Still return product with origin noted.
edge_case_rules.certification_missing: If no certified option exists, apply ingredient/label check as substitute. Note absence of certification in report.
